quizzes.title: Cold War Arms Control Milestones: MCQ Practice
quizzes.passage: Arms control between the United States and the Soviet Union developed through a long series of talks and agreements. The booklet defines disarmament as reducing or eliminating weapons, either unilaterally or mutually, to promote global peace and security. In 1967, US President Lyndon B. Johnson warned that a Soviet missile defence system around Moscow raised the danger of a destabilising first-strike capability. The Strategic Arms Limitation Talks, known as SALT, then produced a set of agreements. The first round ran from 1969 to 1972, and SALT II followed from 1972 to 1979. Later instruments followed. The Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty, known as START I, was concluded in 1991, and START II was negotiated in 1993. The Strategic Offensive Reductions Treaty, or SORT, followed in 2002. Missile defence, delivery systems and warhead numbers were each addressed in different instruments. Each of these agreements is dated and named in the booklet, and the sequence runs from the late 1960s to the early 2000s. The talks took place during Cold War rivalry between the two powers, which is the context in which each instrument was negotiated. The booklet presents these events in chronological order. Taken together, these agreements show how the two powers attempted to manage their nuclear balance over several decades.

questions.q: Which agreement was produced by the first round of the Strategic Arms Limitation Talks (1969-1972)?
questions.explanation: The first SALT round (1969-1972) resulted in the Anti-Ballistic Missile (ABM) Treaty.

questions.q: Why did the United States never ratify SALT II?
options: Russia's withdrawal after the US exit from the ABM Treaty
Cap of 6000 nuclear warheads under START I
questions.explanation: The United States never ratified SALT II owing to Soviet military intervention in Afghanistan.

questions.q: START I (1991) capped nuclear warheads at what number?
questions.explanation: START I capped nuclear warheads at 6000 and also enforced inspections.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): START II collapsed.
Reason (R): Russia withdrew after the United States exited the ABM Treaty.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Russia's withdrawal after the US exit from the ABM Treaty triggered the collapse of START II.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
List I
I. SALT II
II. START I
III. START II
IV. SORT
List II
A. Enforced inspections
B. Also known as the Moscow Treaty
C. Limits on nuclear delivery systems
D. Aim of reducing nuclear weapons to 3,500
questions.explanation: SALT II set limits on delivery systems, START I enforced inspections, START II aimed at 3,500 weapons, and SORT is also known as the Moscow Treaty.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. SORT was an interim agreement between the United States and Russia.
II. START II set a target of 6000 nuclear weapons.
III. START I expired in 2009.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: SORT was an interim agreement and START I expired in 2009, while START II's target was 3,500, not 6000.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The ABM Treaty restricted deployment of missile defence systems.
II. SORT is also known as the New START Treaty.
III. The United States ratified SALT II in 1979.
questions.explanation: Only the first statement is correct, since SORT is the Moscow Treaty and the US never ratified SALT II.

quizzes.title: Cold War Arms Control Milestones: TITA Practice
quizzes.passage: Arms control between the United States and the Soviet Union developed through a sequence of talks, agreements and interim pacts. The booklet defines disarmament as reducing or eliminating weapons, either unilaterally or mutually, to promote global peace and security. In 1967, US President Lyndon B. Johnson warned that a Soviet missile defence system around Moscow raised the danger of a destabilising first-strike capability. The Strategic Arms Limitation Talks, known as SALT, produced agreements that dealt with missile defence and with delivery systems. Some of these agreements were never ratified by one of the two sides, while others were overtaken by later events. The Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty, known as START I, was concluded in 1991. It enforced inspections and capped the number of nuclear warheads, and it was followed in 1993 by START II, which was intended to reduce nuclear weapons further. The booklet notes that START II did not survive in its original form, and it links that outcome to a withdrawal by one of the parties. Missile defence, delivery systems and warhead numbers were each addressed in different instruments. Each agreement is dated and named in the booklet. Taken together, these agreements show how the two powers attempted to manage their nuclear balance over several decades.

questions.q: What maximum number of nuclear warheads was capped under START I (1991)? (number)
questions.explanation: START I capped nuclear warheads at 6000.

questions.q: Which 2002 interim agreement between the US and Russia is also called the Moscow Treaty? (acronym)
questions.explanation: SORT, a 2002 interim agreement, is also known as the Moscow Treaty.

questions.q: Soviet military intervention in which country led the United States never to ratify SALT II? (country)
questions.explanation: The US never ratified SALT II owing to Soviet military intervention in Afghanistan.

questions.q: Which round of the Strategic Arms Limitation Talks (1969-1972) produced the ABM Treaty? (name the round)
questions.explanation: The first SALT round (1969-1972) produced the Anti-Ballistic Missile (ABM) Treaty.

questions.q: Russia withdrew from START II after the United States exited which treaty? (name)
questions.explanation: Russia withdrew after the US exited the ABM Treaty, which triggered the collapse of START II.

questions.q: What number of nuclear weapons did START II (1993) aim to reduce to? (number)
questions.explanation: START II aimed to reduce nuclear weapons to 3,500.

questions.q: In which year did START I (1991) expire? (year)
questions.explanation: START I expired in 2009.

quizzes.title: Nuclear Treaties and Control Regimes: MCQ Practice
quizzes.passage: Global efforts to limit nuclear weapons rest on several separate instruments rather than on one single agreement. The booklet presents a set of treaties related to nuclear disarmament and a set of key nuclear control regimes. These items are arranged in a sequence that begins with the Outer Space Treaty. The booklet also gives a short definition of disarmament, which involves reducing or eliminating weapons either unilaterally or mutually. Others concern the spread of nuclear weapons, and they include the Treaty on Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons, the Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty and the Treaty on Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons. Export regimes such as the Missile Technology Control Regime, the Australia Group and the Wassenaar Arrangement coordinate controls on sensitive goods, so that member states apply shared rules to certain exports. The booklet lists each instrument with its own details, and the instruments were developed over several decades, from the late 1960s onward. On 6 and 9 August 1945, the United States dropped atomic bombs, 'Little Boy' on Hiroshima and 'Fat Man' on Nagasaki, in Japan. The booklet also records India's Pokhran tests of 1974 and 1998 as part of this history. Nuclear-weapon-free zones are regions committed to banning nuclear weapons, and the booklet describes them as part of the same broader topic.

questions.q: Which 1967 instrument bans the deployment of weapons of mass destruction in outer space?
options: Treaty on Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons
questions.explanation: The Outer Space Treaty (1967) bans deployment of weapons of mass destruction in outer space.

questions.q: The Treaty on Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (1968) classifies nations into which two categories?
questions.explanation: The NPT classifies nations as nuclear-weapon states and non-nuclear-weapon states.

questions.q: Why has the Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty (1996) not become operational?
options: The IAEA has rejected its verification role
Ratification by key nuclear-armed states is pending
It was never signed by any country
The United Nations abandoned the treaty
questions.explanation: The CTBT remains non-operational because ratification by key nuclear-armed states is still pending.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Australia Group was formed in 1985 as an informal export control forum.
Reason (R): It was established after chemical weapons were used in the Iran-Iraq War.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: The Australia Group was established after chemical weapons use in the Iran-Iraq War, which is the reason for its formation.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
List I
I. Treaty on Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons
II. Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty
III. Treaty on Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons
IV. Missile Technology Control Regime
List II
A. 1987
B. 2017
C. 1968
D. 1996
questions.explanation: The NPT is dated 1968, the CTBT 1996, the TPNW 2017, and the MTCR 1987.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Missile Technology Control Regime is an informal political understanding.
II. The Treaty on Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons permits states that have signed it to possess nuclear weapons.
III. The Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty seeks to ban nuclear weapon testing for civilian and military use.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The MTCR is an informal understanding and the CTBT seeks a testing ban, while the TPNW bans rather than permits possession.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Wassenaar Arrangement promotes transparency in conventional arms and dual-use exports.
II. The Australia Group is a formal treaty with binding inspection rules.
III. The Treaty on Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons bans the development of nuclear weapons.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while the Australia Group is an informal forum rather than a formal treaty.

quizzes.title: Nuclear Treaties and Control Regimes: TITA Practice
quizzes.passage: Nuclear arms control is pursued through a network of global instruments rather than a single agreement. Some of these instruments are treaties, while others are informal understandings or export-control arrangements. The booklet groups its subjects under headings for nuclear disarmament treaties and nuclear control regimes. Disarmament, as the booklet explains it, involves reducing or eliminating weapons, either unilaterally or mutually, to promote global peace and security. Some instruments deal with the spread of nuclear weapons, and others deal with testing. A further group of arrangements coordinates national controls on goods that could be used in weapons programmes. The booklet also recalls the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945, which were carried out by the United States. Its account of India's nuclear history includes the Pokhran tests of 1974 and 1998. The booklet presents a chronology of nuclear events, beginning with the 1945 bombings and continuing through the treaties. The booklet describes the International Atomic Energy Agency as an organisation that monitors peaceful nuclear programmes, and it was established in 1957. It states that the agency assists nations in using nuclear technology. Nuclear-weapon-free zones are regions committed to banning nuclear weapons, and the booklet describes them alongside the instruments listed above.

questions.q: Which 1967 treaty bans the deployment of weapons of mass destruction in outer space? (name of the treaty)
questions.explanation: The Outer Space Treaty of 1967 bans deployment of weapons of mass destruction in outer space.

questions.q: Which 1968 treaty classifies nations as nuclear-weapon or non-nuclear-weapon states? (short form)
accept: Treaty on Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons
Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons
questions.explanation: The NPT classifies nations as nuclear-weapon or non-nuclear-weapon states.

questions.q: In which year was the Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty concluded? (year)
questions.explanation: The CTBT (1996) seeks to ban all nuclear weapon testing for civilian and military use.

questions.q: In which year was the Treaty on Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons concluded? (year)
questions.explanation: The Treaty on Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons is dated 2017.

questions.q: Which informal political understanding of 1987 aims to prevent proliferation of missiles and UAVs capable of delivering weapons of mass destruction? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The MTCR is an informal political understanding of 1987 aimed at preventing missile and UAV proliferation.

questions.q: Which 1985 informal export control forum was formed after chemical weapons were used in the Iran-Iraq War? (name)
questions.explanation: The Australia Group was established in 1985 after chemical weapons use in the Iran-Iraq War.

questions.q: Which 1996 voluntary export control regime promotes transparency in conventional arms and dual-use exports? (name)
questions.explanation: The Wassenaar Arrangement (1996) is a voluntary export control regime.
